data.body:
Operator decision (2026-08-19): APPROVED — run the op-cert container as a FIXED non-root UID, and change the compose bind-mount ownership for the 0600 private key in the SAME change so both halves deploy together.

Rationale: the coupling between the container UID and the mounted key's owner IS the whole risk here. Splitting it across two changes is precisely what breaks the deploy — the signer fails to start when the UID cannot read the key. A build-arg UID was considered and rejected as adding per-environment configuration surface (and a new way to get it wrong) for no benefit at this scale. Staying root was rejected: it leaves the S6 hardening advisory permanently open.

Implementation must therefore touch infra/Dockerfile.opcert (USER + fixed UID) and infra/compose (mount ownership) atomically, and the change should state the chosen UID explicitly so the deploy is reproducible.
